content.comment_body: Thank you for the guidance. How can I access three [product_name] units on my local network? Which port does each [product_name] use, and how can I reach different IP addresses on my LAN from outside the network? Thanks, [user_name]

It's likely not possible to change the TCP port the [product_name] units use for communication. However, you can set up multiple address translations on your firewall to direct traffic to various internal IPs, either by using multiple public IP addresses or, if you only have one public IP, by mapping multiple ports on your router to the respective private IPs. Option 1: Public IP 1 -> 192.168.1.10, Public IP 2 -> 192.168.1.11. You'd then access them by entering http://[Public IP 1] in your browser. Option 2: Public IP:81 -> 192.168.1.10, Public IP:82 -> 192.168.1.11. In this case, you'd reach them using http://[Public IP]:81 in your browser.

analysis.insight_summary: Users aim to connect to several [product_name] devices on their LAN and need to understand network protocol and port configuration for remote access. The main challenge is determining how to distinguish and access multiple [product_name] modules externally, especially since port customization on these devices appears unavailable.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks a method to reach multiple [product_name] units on their LAN from outside the network, preferably by using distinct IP addresses or ports, as well as clear instructions on which ports are required and how to configure the network accordingly.
